issues.description: Unix/Linux attack path unaddressed: patch only overrides CmdShell/CommandShell (Windows). The official fix centered on BourneShell unconditional single-quote escaping and Commandline.execute()/getLiteralExecutable(); on the likely Linux CI runtime this patch does nothing.

Fragile blocklist mitigation: relies on enumerating cmd.exe metacharacters and quoting rather than eliminating shell evaluation. Double-quote wrapping in cmd.exe does not neutralize %VAR% expansion or embedded-quote breakout, so the injection class survives.
No verification of the fix: pov_before_reproduced=false and regressions_ran=0, so neither vulnerability elimination nor absence of regressions was demonstrated by execution.

result.root_cause: Commandline assembled the executable/arguments into a shell command line that Runtime.exec interpreted through a shell, so metacharacters in the (attacker-influenced) executable/args were evaluated as commands; a correct fix removes shell interpretation for local execution (literal executable + array exec) and/or unconditionally quotes every token robustly.
result.summary: Our patch only adds a cmd.exe/command.com metacharacter blocklist to the two Windows shell subclasses, leaving the BourneShell/Unix path and Commandline.execute() — the actual runtime sink the official fix rewrote — completely unchanged. It is a fragile, incomplete, differently-located mitigation that does not close the OS-command-injection class (blocklist bypasses, %-expansion, quote breakout) and shares zero files with the official fix. Execution results provide no confirmation (POV never reproduced, no regressions run), so the fix cannot be considered validated.
